The Quantum Γ-Turing machine considered here retains a finite-dimensional register’s trace-norm limit when it exists, preserving the coherence needed by subsequent operations. Averaging a history that never settles permits another continuation, although registers independent at every finite stage can then acquire correlations through their shared timing. We characterise when an assigned state can replace its history without changing a later joint calculation. For assignments compatible with every fixed quantum operation, the largest composition error equals the mean trace-norm distance from the assigned state, and a partner carrying classical labels can approach that value. Independent composition with every partner holds precisely when temporal variance under the chosen mean vanishes. Requiring this under every shift-invariant mean gives uniform vanishing of average squared fluctuations, a condition that permits sparse excursions despite failure of ordinary convergence. For a programme repeatedly applying one fixed channel, independent composition is instead equivalent to ordinary convergence, with the exact error determined by its surviving nonstationary spectral component. Algebraically specified channels and initial states admit a finite decision procedure and certified bounds, while bounded repetitions of states preserve the stronger averaging condition and transfer its certificates to a simulation. These results connect transfinite continuation to finite verification for specified programmes and provide composition certificates that can be carried through a controlled simulation.

summary: Per distruggere la Rotta dei Chersoneso, venne fatta la Battaglia di Cheronea https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battaglia_di_Cheronea_(87_a.C.) Per distruggere i commerci con Etruschi e Cartaginesi, venne fatta la Battaglia di Alalia https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battaglia_del_Mare_Sardo Per distruggere i rapporti con la Facies Sarda dei Bessi di Perperikon, venne fatta la battaglia del Monte Emo:   La battaglia del Monte Emo (o Haemus ) è storicamente legata a due momenti distinti dell'antichità che videro scontrarsi gli eserciti invasori con le tribù tracie, in particolare i Bessi , e il cui contesto geografico e spirituale è strettamente connesso al celebre sito monumentale di Perperikon , situato nelle montagne dei Rodopi in Bulgaria. [ 1 , 2 ] Ecco come si collegano questi tre elementi:   1. La prima battaglia del Monte Emo (335 a.C.) Prima di lanciare la sua campagna contro i Persiani, Alessandro Magno guidò una spedizione nei Balcani per rendere sicuri i confini settentrionali del suo regno. Sul Monte Emo (l'attuale catena dei Monti Balcani) affrontò i Traci Liberi e altre tribù locali. [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] La tattica dei carri: I Traci si erano posizionati sulla vetta e intendevano far rotolare dei pesanti carri giù dai ripidi pendii per rompere la falange macedone. [ 1 , 2 ] La contromossa di Alessandro: Il re macedone ordinò ai suoi soldati di aprire i ranghi per far passare i carri oppure di sdraiarsi a terra coprendosi con gli scudi intersecati (creando una sorta di testuggine). La tattica funzionò alla perfezione: i carri rimbalzarono sugli scudi senza causare vittime tra i Macedoni. Le truppe di Alessandro caricarono poi la vetta, sbaragliando i difensori. [ 1 , 2 , 3 ]   2. Lo scontro dei Bessi con Roma (72 a.C.) In epoca successiva, il nome della battaglia del Monte Emo si associa alla sottomissione definitiva dei Bessi , una delle tribù tracie più bellicose e fanaticamente dedite al culto religioso. Il proconsole romano Marco Licinio Lucullo affrontò i Bessi proprio nei pressi della catena del Monte Emo, sconfiggendoli duramente in una grande battaglia campale, conquistando il loro centro principale ( Uscudama ) e aprendo la strada alla successiva egemonia romana nella regione. [ 1 , 2 , 3 ]   3. Il legame con Perperikon La tribù dei Bessi era storicamente la custode del famosissimo Santuario e Oracolo di Dioniso , situato proprio sulla maestosa roccia sacra di Perperikon . Questo luogo ha un valore storico eccezionale per due importanti profezie collegate ai protagonisti di queste guerre: [ 1 , 2 ] La profezia di Alessandro Magno: Secondo le fonti antiche, prima di iniziare la sua spedizione in Asia (subito dopo aver pacificato la Tracia), Alessandro visitò l'oracolo di Dioniso a Perperikon. Il vino versato sull'altare creò una fiammata altissima fino al cielo, un segno divino che i sacerdoti interpretarono come il presagio che avrebbe conquistato il mondo intero. [ 1 ] La profezia di Ottaviano Augusto: Anni dopo, anche il padre di Augusto (Gaio Ottavio) ricevette nello stesso santuario dei Bessi la medesima profezia sul futuro dominio globale di suo figlio. [ 1 ] In sintesi, la resistenza dei Traci sul Monte Emo rappresenta lo scontro militare per il controllo dei Balcani, mentre Perperikon costituisce il cuore spirituale, politico e identitario della tribù dei Bessi che contro quegli imperi tentò invano di difendere la propria indipendenza. [ 1 , 2 ]   Attenzione: questo documento è stato appena pensato: si tratta di una bozza iniziale basata sul Paradigma Sardo Corso Atlantideo di Luigi Usai. summary: Code and country-level derived data that reproduce the results of “Disembedding or Persistent Embeddedness? Testing Polanyi against Granovetter.” Python scripts build a respondent extract from the WVS Trend File 1981–2022 (v4.1) and the EVS Trend File 1981–2017 (ZA7503 v3.0.0), which users must download from the World Values Survey Association and GESIS under their own terms. They also build country-level files from the Fraser Institute EFW Panel Dataset (2026) and the OECD Social Expenditure Database. A Stata 19.5 do-file reproduces Tables 3 and 4 and Figure 2. The respondent-level survey data are not redistributed.

summary: Deepwave provides wave propagation modules for PyTorch, for applications such as seismic imaging and inversion. It performs forward modelling and backpropagation, so it can simulate wave propagation to generate synthetic data, or invert for the scattering potential (reverse-time migration, RTM, or its least-squares counterpart, LSRTM), other model parameters (full-waveform inversion, FWI), initial wavefields, or source wavelets. It can also be used inside a larger chain of operations, with forward and backpropagation flowing through the whole chain end to end. You can use your own objective functions, or functions that generate the propagator's inputs, and PyTorch's automatic differentiation calculates how to backpropagate through them. New to seismic/wave-equation terminology? The glossary defines the terms (PML, CFL, Born, FWI, and more) used throughout this README and the rest of the documentation. Deepwave requires Python 3.9 or later and PyTorch 2.4 or later. First install PyTorch for your CPU or CUDA device using the instructions on the PyTorch website . Then install Deepwave: pip install deepwave   macOS wheels support Apple Silicon. Intel Mac wheels are no longer provided: PyTorch 2.4 and newer do not publish wheels for that platform. Prebuilt x86 wheels require AVX2. Older CPUs need a source build; see installation troubleshooting . PyTorch is Deepwave's only dependency. The example scripts under docs/ additionally import matplotlib (to draw their figures) and, in some cases, numpy , scipy (smoothing and filter design), torchaudio (applying those filters), torchvision and geomloss , but those are needed only to run the examples, never by Deepwave itself. To install all of them: pip install 'deepwave[examples]'   The documentation contains examples and instructions on how to install and use Deepwave. You might also like to watch a video summary of Deepwave . Not every propagator supports every option (dimensionality, backend, boundary faces, batching, second-order differentiation, callbacks, ...). See the capability matrix (declared in the code and checked by conformance tests) before assuming a combination works. Why Deepwave Computationally efficient. Deepwave's compiled kernels use a hand-derived adjoint for better performance and lower memory requirements than pure PyTorch implementations. See what Deepwave calculates . Second derivatives are supported, not just first. The scalar, acoustic, and elastic propagators can compute Hessian-vector products (derivatives of gradients); see the Hessian example . Born (linearised) modelling. Model scattered waves from perturbations to a background medium for linearised inversion and imaging. See the torch.func example . Deepwave fits into an ordinary PyTorch workflow. Because propagation is a normal PyTorch autograd Function , it works directly with PyTorch optimisers, DistributedDataParallel over shots, torch.func transforms, and any PyTorch loss function or neural-network model of the input parameters. See the capability matrix for exactly what each propagator supports. Deepwave does not try to be a general symbolic PDE solver, a multi-node HPC code, or a non-differentiable simulation toolkit — see Devito , SPECFEM , and k-Wave respectively for those needs. If you are choosing between wave-propagation packages, see the comparison guide . (Note: the DeepWave-KAUST GitHub organisation, home of the SWEEP package, is unrelated to this project.) Features Supports the 1D, 2D, and 3D constant density acoustic / scalar wave equation (regular and Born modelling), variable density acoustic, elastic, viscoacoustic (single-mechanism SLS attenuation), elastic VTI (anisotropic), and pseudo-acoustic VTI ( deepwave.acoustic_vti , the Duveneck et al. 2008 V_S=0 reduction) wave equations Runs on CPUs and appropriate GPUs The gradient of all outputs (final wavefields and receiver data) can be calculated with respect to the model parameters (wavespeed, scattering potential, etc

direction_title: Rowan / BBC1 protein structural confidence vs experimental stability falsification [COUNTEREVIDENCE]
summary: Disease surveillance increasingly integrates automated data collection, yet predefined sources and procedures require manual adaptation as reporting practices change. We explore agentic artificial intelligence (AI) as an approach to coordinating surveillance data collection across heterogeneous sources. Specifically, we built a multi-agent framework that integrates source discovery, source assessment, evidence structuring, event linking, and validation. Three retrospective applications illustrate its promise. The workflow recovered all 13 individual cases in a hantavirus outbreak, with links to 85 distinct publisher domains compared with 28 in the reference benchmark, reconstructed Canadian measles counts with a final total 0.33% below the national reference and higher cumulative counts on 79.8% of comparable days, and increased the share of days with recent Sierra Leone mpox reports from 28.2% to 65.6% by incorporating attributed media. These demonstrations also reveal limitations in record completeness and accuracy, while prospective gains in timeliness remain untested. We envision agentic AI as a complementary layer of public health data infrastructure, coordinating evidence-linked collection under surveillance goals and standards defined by public health professionals.
title: Toward an Agentic AI Approach to Public Health Data Collection

summary: Pre-built per-gene covariate matrices for TCGA-READ (Rectum adenocarcinoma. Biologically and genomically the same disease as COAD (TCGA's own marker paper pooled them as COADREAD), so every covariate source is COAD's, re-verified 2026-10-03: GTEx maps to the colon tissues (representative Colon_Transverse_Mucosa, the epithelial cell of origin; GTEx has no rectum). summary: TEMPLATE-DIRECTED MASS FABRICATION OF BIOMEDICAL MICRO/NANOROBOTS AT THE LIMIT is a 770-page, high-density English research monograph on scaling template replication without losing dimensional fidelity, surface integrity, functional consistency or scientific traceability. The book treats the template as a stateful manufacturing ancestor rather than a passive tool. Every cavity and replication cycle is registered so that template wear, release-coating decay, demolding force, replica bias, particle residue, spatial defect clustering and functional outcomes can be linked across the full template life. Its central falsifiable claim asks whether lifetime-aware monitoring can predict rising defect probability before damage spreads. Thirty mathematically distinct research plates cover cavity filling, squeeze flow, material relaxation, cure conversion, shrinkage, residual stress, adhesion, demolding, fracture, Archard wear, coating survival, hidden wear states, geometry transfer, Hausdorff error, spatial point processes, defect ancestry, survival hazards, change points, capability, conservative yield, hierarchical variance and qualified-part cost. Across 82 chapters and 410 single-page studies, the monograph develops replication physics, release mechanics, template wear, spatial defect genealogy, adaptive process control, functional qualification, lifecycle economics and independent transfer. Two hundred Research Gates define blind challenges, strong comparators, evidence packages, hard stops and successor forks. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos present genuinely different witnesses, challenge artifacts, estimators, controllers, economic falsifiers, release keys and handoff kits. The work is explicitly nonclinical and hypothesis-generating. It does not claim a completed manufacturing campaign, human treatment, autonomous in-body efficacy or regulatory approval. Its release rule is conjunctive: wear, demolding force, geometry, defect clustering, unselected yield, task function and traceability must pass together over the complete template life. Author: Feng Cheng-en (33) x Starli Series: STARLI Research Institute XXXIV / Flagship 09 Edition: Research Working Edition v1.0 / October 2026

summary: A Turing machine carries a computation forward through successive configurations, but continuation beyond infinitely many steps requires a rule assigning the configuration from which the next instruction can proceed. The Quantum Γ-Turing machine considered here retains a finite-dimensional register’s trace-norm limit when it exists, preserving the coherence needed by subsequent operations. Averaging a history that never settles permits another continuation, although registers independent at every finite stage can then acquire correlations through their shared timing. We characterise when an assigned state can replace its history without changing a later joint calculation. For assignments compatible with every fixed quantum operation, the largest composition error equals the mean trace-norm distance from the assigned state, and a partner carrying classical labels can approach that value. Independent composition with every partner holds precisely when temporal variance under the chosen mean vanishes. Requiring this under every shift-invariant mean gives uniform vanishing of average squared fluctuations, a condition that permits sparse excursions despite failure of ordinary convergence. For a programme repeatedly applying one fixed channel, independent composition is instead equivalent to ordinary convergence, with the exact error determined by its surviving nonstationary spectral component. Algebraically specified channels and initial states admit a finite decision procedure and certified bounds, while bounded repetitions of states preserve the stronger averaging condition and transfer its certificates to a simulation. These results connect transfinite continuation to finite verification for specified programmes and provide composition certificates that can be carried through a controlled simulation.
title: Independent Composition and Quantum Limits in Transfinite Γ-Turing Machines

summary: Deepwave provides wave propagation modules for PyTorch, for applications such as seismic imaging and inversion. It performs forward modelling and backpropagation, so it can simulate wave propagation to generate synthetic data, or invert for the scattering potential (reverse-time migration, RTM, or its least-squares counterpart, LSRTM), other model parameters (full-waveform inversion, FWI), initial wavefields, or source wavelets. It can also be used inside a larger chain of operations, with forward and backpropagation flowing through the whole chain end to end. You can use your own objective functions, or functions that generate the propagator's inputs, and PyTorch's automatic differentiation calculates how to backpropagate through them. New to seismic/wave-equation terminology? The glossary defines the terms (PML, CFL, Born, FWI, and more) used throughout this README and the rest of the documentation. Deepwave requires Python 3.9 or later and PyTorch 2.4 or later. First install PyTorch for your CPU or CUDA device using the instructions on the PyTorch website . Then install Deepwave: pip install deepwave   macOS wheels support Apple Silicon. Intel Mac wheels are no longer provided: PyTorch 2.4 and newer do not publish wheels for that platform. Prebuilt x86 wheels require AVX2. Older CPUs need a source build; see installation troubleshooting . PyTorch is Deepwave's only dependency. The example scripts under docs/ additionally import matplotlib (to draw their figures) and, in some cases, numpy , scipy (smoothing and filter design), torchaudio (applying those filters), torchvision and geomloss , but those are needed only to run the examples, never by Deepwave itself. To install all of them: pip install 'deepwave[examples]'   The documentation contains examples and instructions on how to install and use Deepwave. You might also like to watch a video summary of Deepwave . Not every propagator supports every option (dimensionality, backend, boundary faces, batching, second-order differentiation, callbacks, ...). See the capability matrix (declared in the code and checked by conformance tests) before assuming a combination works. Why Deepwave Computationally efficient. Deepwave's compiled kernels use a hand-derived adjoint for better performance and lower memory requirements than pure PyTorch implementations. See what Deepwave calculates . Second derivatives are supported, not just first. The scalar, acoustic, and elastic propagators can compute Hessian-vector products (derivatives of gradients); see the Hessian example . Born (linearised) modelling. Model scattered waves from perturbations to a background medium for linearised inversion and imaging. See the torch.func example . Deepwave fits into an ordinary PyTorch workflow. Because propagation is a normal PyTorch autograd Function , it works directly with PyTorch optimisers, DistributedDataParallel over shots, torch.func transforms, and any PyTorch loss function or neural-network model of the input parameters. See the capability matrix for exactly what each propagator supports. Deepwave does not try to be a general symbolic PDE solver, a multi-node HPC code, or a non-differentiable simulation toolkit — see Devito , SPECFEM , and k-Wave respectively for those needs. If you are choosing between wave-propagation packages, see the comparison guide . (Note: the DeepWave-KAUST GitHub organisation, home of the SWEEP package, is unrelated to this project.) Features Supports the 1D, 2D, and 3D constant density acoustic / scalar wave equation (regular and Born modelling), variable density acoustic, elastic, viscoacoustic (single-mechanism SLS attenuation), elastic VTI (anisotropic), and pseudo-acoustic VTI ( deepwave.acoustic_vti , the Duveneck et al. 2008 V_S=0 reduction) wave equations Runs on CPUs and appropriate GPUs The gradient of all outputs (final wavefields and receiver data) can be calculated with respect to the model parameters (wavespeed, scattering potential, etc
title: Deepwave

summary: Data and R code that reproduce all tables and figures of the article "Dependence on China, Export Volatility and Relationship Persistence: Shipment-Level Evidence from Peruvian Copper Ore, 2006–2025", of its Appendix A and of its Supplementary Material.   Version 1.1.0 accompanies the revised manuscript (first review round). It keeps all data, code and outputs of version 1.0.0, which are reproduced identically, and adds the scripts, data and outputs of the analyses carried out in the revision: Cox models stratified by firm, with shared frailty and with a firm random effect, and without Chinese-owned firms; a firm-level (granular) and a Shapley decomposition of aggregate export volatility; a destination counterfactual; seasonality checks; regime-specific concentration coefficients; destination concentration by net weight; sensitivity analyses and a shift-share instrument for the firm–year panel; mirror statistics from UN Comtrade (imports of HS 2603 reported by China and the Republic of Korea); and a comparison of the extract with SUNAT's published statistics (Tables G8 and G9).   The package contains the shipment-level extract of Peruvian exports of copper ores and concentrates (HS 2603.00.00.00) from PromPerú's Infotrade platform, based on SUNAT export customs declarations, January 2006 – December 2025, validated month by month against PromPerú's official totals (23,106 shipments; 22,582 commercial shipments by 200 firms to 44 destinations, USD 219.3 billion FOB, in the analysis), together with the auxiliary data, the processed datasets and all outputs. A single script (run_all.R) runs the whole pipeline.   Exporters who are natural persons (18 of 266 RUCs; 90 shipments) are pseudonymized; the replacement is one-to-one and does not change any result. The firm–destination–month dataset obtained from SUNAT through an access-to-information request, used only for cross-validation, is not redistributed. See README.md for details.
title: Data and R code for: Dependence on China, Export Volatility and Relationship Persistence: Shipment-Level Evidence from Peruvian Copper Ore, 2006–2025

summary: Öz   Bu çalışmanın amacı, genç erkek basketbolcularda Fonksiyonel Hareket Tarama (FMS) toplam ve alt test puanları ile alt ekstremite denge asimetrisi arasındaki ilişkileri ve bu puanların asimetriyi yordama düzeyini incelemektir. Kesitsel ve ilişkisel tarama modelinde tasarlanan araştırmaya, yaş ortalaması 18,90 ± 1,21 yıl ve spor yaşı ortalaması 7,83 ± 1,77 yıl olan 52 gönüllü lisanslı erkek basketbolcu katılmıştır. Fonksiyonel hareketler yedi alt testten oluşan FMS ile değerlendirilmiştir. Alt testler 0–3 arasında puanlanmış ve toplam puan 21 puan üzerinden değerlendirilmiştir. Dinamik denge, anterior, posteromedial ve posterolateral uzanma yönlerini içeren Y-Denge Testi (YBT) ile ölçülmüştür. Her iki alt ekstremiteden elde edilen uzanma mesafeleri kullanılarak taraflara ait bileşik puanlar hesaplanmış ve denge asimetri yüzdesi analiz edilmiştir. Verilerin analizinde betimsel istatistikler, Pearson korelasyon analizi ve çoklu doğrusal regresyon analizi kullanılmıştır. FMS toplam puanı ile asimetri yüzdesi (r = −0,059), dominant bileşik puan (r = −0,031) ve non-dominant bileşik puan (r = −0,013) arasında anlamlı ilişki bulunmamıştır (p > 0,05). Asimetri yüzdesi ile dominant bileşik puan arasında çok güçlü pozitif ilişki saptanmıştır (r = 0,921; p < 0,01). FMS toplam ve alt test puanlarını içeren regresyon modeli genel olarak anlamlı değildir (R² = 0,256; düzeltilmiş R² = 0,117; p = 0,094). Modelde gövde stabilitesi şınavının (TSPU) katsayısı negatif (β = −0,399; p = 0,015), omuz mobilitesinin (SM) katsayısı ise pozitif yönde anlamlı bulunmuştur (β = 0,342; p = 0,049). Diğer alt testlerin ve toplam puanın katsayıları anlamlı değildir (p > 0,05). Sonuç olarak, FMS toplam puanı bu örneklemde denge asimetrisiyle anlamlı bir ilişki göstermemiştir. Bulgular, basketbolcuların değerlendirilmesinde yalnızca toplam FMS puanına odaklanılmaması gerektiğini; alt test sonuçlarının ve taraflara özgü dinamik denge ölçümlerinin birlikte ele alınması gerektiğini göstermektedir.   Anahtar Kelimeler: Basketbol, Fonksiyonel Hareket Taraması, Dinamik Denge, Ekstremiteler Arası Asimetri, Gövde Stabilitesi   Abstract The relationship between the Functional Movement Screen (FMS) total and individual test scores and the asymmetry of balance of the lower extremities, as well as the predictive effect on young male basketball players, was analysed in this study. This was a cross-sectional correlational study that consisted of 52 licensed male basketball players volunteering for the study at the age of 18.90 ± 1.21 years and having a sport experience of 7.83 ± 1.77 years. The assessment of functional movement was carried out through the seven FMS tests. These tests were individually scored in range of 0 to 3 points with a maximal total of 21 points. Reach distances for both lower extremities were used to calculate limb-specific composite scores, and balance asymmetry percentage was analyzed. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression were used. FMS total score was not significantly correlated with asymmetry percentage (r = −0.059), dominant composite score (r = −0.031), or non-dominant composite score (r = −0.013; all p > 0.05). Asymmetry percentage showed a very strong positive correlation with dominant composite score (r = 0.921; p < 0.01). The regression model including FMS total and individual test scores was not statistically significant overall (R² = 0.256; adjusted R² = 0.117; p = 0.094). Within this model, trunk stability push-up (TSPU) had a significant negative coefficient (β = −0.399; p = 0.015), whereas shoulder mobility (SM) had a significant positive coeff
title: Genç Basketbolcularda Fonksiyonel Hareket Analizi Skorlarının Denge Asimetrisi Üzerindeki Yordayıcı Rolü

summary: This record preserves the v0.2.0 trained-model weight bundle for takotsubo_ami_ai_ecg. It contains selected ViT, ConvNeXtV2 and MLP-Mixer inference tensors in safetensors format, ViT configuration files, a manifest, and the applicable license texts and notices. These research models classify prepared ECG images as takotsubo syndrome or acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The file takotsubo_ami_ai_ecg_weights_v0.2.0.zip is the unchanged GitHub release asset: 958,701,120 bytes, SHA-256 cba7d135b1e2f5491f1c0ccab93aef8e3b65570586f8052029540b94e7fbf510. It contains 11 files, including three model.safetensors files. Patient images, training datasets, prediction tables, participant records, optimizer state and original training-machine paths are excluded. The selected source states are ViT checkpoint-6900/model.safetensors and the ordinary model states from ckpt_0011.pth for ConvNeXtV2 and MLP-Mixer. The ConvNeXtV2 SWA checkpoint and SWA state are not used for the default inference path. Training and validation loss curves were reviewed, and the checkpoint with the lowest validation loss among epochs without apparent signs of overfitting was selected. This describes the reported selection procedure and does not prove that overfitting was absent. Use the companion software release v0.3.0 for command-line or Colab inference and optional ViT/ConvNeXtV2 Grad-CAM output. The default input is a prepared 480 x 480 image, and the class order is tako, AMI. Paper-default TTA uses ViT 24 views/magnitude 1, ConvNeXtV2 one unchanged view, and MLP-Mixer 32 views/magnitude 3. Each model's view logits are averaged; the ensemble averages the three models' raw logits with equal weights before applying softmax. The selected inference tensors were checked against their original source tensors, and the published bundle and its member-file hashes were verified. Software checks include the documented ten-image no-TTA comparison and synthetic-image paper-TTA execution. These checks do not establish clinical accuracy, historical stochastic-TTA equivalence, complete training reproduction, or equivalence to historical reader-study visualizations. See the dated validation scope (https://github.com/ekagawa007/takotsubo_ami_ai_ecg/blob/f8553b994cc8f3ac99c5e7e3ed44cea312dde512/docs/implementation_status.md). Retain the original MAE noncommercial notice and the Hugging Face distribution's Apache-2.0 notice. Commercially unrestricted use of the ViT assets is not granted. ConvNeXtV2 and MLP-Mixer weights: the author's contributions are licensed under MIT, subject to the documented upstream notices. The complete bundle includes the ViT assets and must respect their noncommercial terms. The separate MIT terms for the other author-owned contributions remain unchanged. Retain WEIGHTS_LICENSE.md, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and all accompanying license texts. The saved checkpoint configuration does not identify an immutable upstream model revision; the provenance is not a complete reconstruction of every training step. These materials are intended for research. Clinical accuracy, reliability and fitness for clinical use are not warranted. summary: Replication package for the paper "Risk, not sunshine: financing costs drive the price of reliable solar-plus-storage electricity in the Middle East and North Africa" (Younas Khan and Štefan Bojnec). WHAT THIS IS Code, input data, result tables, figures and a supplementary data workbook for an hourly solar-plus-battery cost comparison of 19 Middle East and North African countries (24 sites: the 19 capitals plus five interior desert sites). The study decomposes the cross-country cost gap into cost of capital, regional equipment price and solar yield, and tests the result against finance shocks, 24 weather years, CMIP6 climate change and Monte Carlo uncertainty. The manuscript itself is not part of this deposit. CONTENTS - code/: all analysis scripts (photovoltaic model, hourly dispatch and design search, climate factors, 24-weather-year test, build-out link, decomposition, bootstrap, Monte Carlo, figures, supplementary tables) and run_all.sh, which reproduces everything in about 6 minutes on one core. - data/inputs/: the input data the scripts read (NASA POWER weather, CMIP6 point extracts, IRENA and SIPRI data, demand and footprint indicators). - results/: result tables (CSV) and results.json, which holds every number quoted in the paper. - outputs/Supplementary_Data.xlsx: a workbook with one sheet for each supplementary table (S1–S26). - outputs/figures/: the figures generated by the code (PNG and PDF). - README.md: step-by-step instructions, a map from each figure and table to its script, and the provenance and terms of each input file. HOW TO REUSE Install the packages in requirements.txt (Python 3.13), then run ./run_all.sh. All random draws use fixed seeds, so a rerun with the default 2,000 Monte Carlo draws reproduces results.json. LICENCE AND THIRD-PARTY DATA The code is released under the MIT licence and the derived results and workbook under CC BY 4.0. Input files from NASA POWER, IRENA, SIPRI, Ember and the Copernicus Climate Data Store keep the terms of their providers and must be cited to the original sources (see README.md). KNOWN LIMITS Costs of capital for Algeria, Libya, Palestine, Syria and Yemen and all hydrogen-chain costs are placeholders; hourly load is assumed, not measured; each country is represented by one reference site. These are documented in Supplementary Tables S20–S22. VERSIONS Version 1.1.0 contains the files listed above. Further datasets will be added as new versions of this record or as separate records linked to it.

summary: SimilCode Benchmark is a curated dataset of 120 short source-code snippets in C# and Java, organised into 60 test-case pairs per language across four ground-truth similarity categories (identical, functional, structural, and different) with fifteen reference groups per language. Every pair was independently classified by two raters blind to the original labels, with near-perfect inter-rater agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.989). All code was authored specifically for this study or drawn from the public domain; no student-submitted code is included. The dataset was used to benchmark four contemporary commercial large language models as similarity analysts — claude-opus-5 , gpt-5.5-2026-04-23 , gemini-3.1-pro-preview and deepseek-v4-pro — with three independent replicates per case–model combination, yielding 1,440 evaluations. The same 120 pairs were also processed with three established classical detectors drawn from three distinct algorithmic families: Moss (winnowing fingerprints), JPlag v6.3.0 (token-string matching) and Dolos v2.9.3 (tree-sitter syntax trees). The record further includes a separate corpus for validating algorithmic-complexity (Big O) estimation: 40 canonical algorithms and 8 adversarial cases designed to defeat surface cues such as misleading identifiers, unreachable code and memoisation. Raw model responses, classical-detector outputs, the standardised prompt with its SHA-256 checksum, the ground-truth tables and the analysis scripts are published together for reproducibility.
title: SimilCode Benchmark: A Dual-Language Source-Code Similarity Dataset for the Evaluation of AI-Based Detectors

summary: This record archives version 0.3.0 of takotsubo_ami_ai_ecg, research software for classifying prepared electrocardiogram (ECG) images as takotsubo syndrome or acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The source archive corresponds to GitHub tag v0.3.0 at commit 341ac955353f535fb74a4b6d8005a8b3b1290ad4. The repository includes retained model-development and evaluation sources, an inference command-line interface, an English Google Colab example, and optional Grad-CAM output for ViT and ConvNeXtV2. It supports ViT, ConvNeXtV2 and MLP-Mixer predictions and their three-model ensemble. Trained model weights are distributed separately as weight release v0.2.0. The default inference input is an already prepared 480 x 480 pixel image. Supported single-frame formats are PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF and WebP; the loader converts images to RGB. Other dimensions are rejected unless the explicit resize option is selected. Resizing alone does not reproduce the study's upstream ECG preparation. Patient ECG images, training datasets and participant records are not included. Paper-default test-time augmentation (TTA) uses 24 views with magnitude 1 for ViT, one unchanged view (no TTA) for ConvNeXtV2, and 32 views with magnitude 3 for MLP-Mixer. View counts include the unchanged image. Raw logits are averaged across each model's views, followed by an equal-weight mean of the three models' raw logits and softmax. Class order is tako, AMI; AMI denotes the acute anterior STEMI comparison group. Defaults include float32 precision, seed 1234, batch size 1 and four workers. TTA results can depend on the execution environment and data-loading configuration. Grad-CAM maps use a separate unaugmented float32 pass for each visualized model. summary: Objectives. Autoimmune hypothyroidism is associated with disturbances in lipid metabolism. This study assessed lipid profiles and cardiovascular risk markers in patients with overt (OH) and subclinical hypothyroidism (SH) compared with healthy controls, and examined lipid changes during levothyroxine treatment. Methods. This observational case–control study included 129 adults: 65 patients with autoimmune hypothyroidism (35 OH, 30 SH) and 64 controls. All patients had complete lipid, TSH, and fT4 measurements at baseline, 8 weeks, and 16 weeks. Lipid indices included LDL cholesterol (LDL-c), HDL cholesterol (HDL-c), non-HDL cholesterol (non-HDL-c), and the total cholesterol/HDL-c ratio. Between-group comparisons and paired longitudinal tests were performed; longitudinal p values were not adjusted for multiple comparisons. Results. Baseline LDL-c was higher in patients than controls (3.96 ± 1.67 vs 3.39 ± 0.76 mmol/L; p = 0.015). Non-HDL-c was higher in OH than SH (5.31 ± 2.19 vs 3.64 ± 0.96 mmol/L), and the total cholesterol/HDL-c ratio was higher in patients than controls (4.16 ± 1.59 vs 3.42 ± 0.75; p = 0.001). At 16 weeks, mean LDL-c decreased from 3.96 ± 1.67 to 3.28 ± 1.00 mmol/L (p = 0.001), and non-HDL-c from 4.54 ± 1.92 to 3.68 ± 1.17 mmol/L (p < 0.001). HDL-c did not improve significantly. At week 16, TSH was within the reference interval in 42 of 65 patients (64.6%). Conclusions. Overt autoimmune hypothyroidism was associated with a more atherogenic lipid profile than SH or euthyroid status. During levothyroxine treatment, LDL-c and non-HDL-c improved, particularly in OH, while HDL-c did not. These observational findings do not establish a causal treatment effect or a reduction in cardiovascular events.
title: LIPID PROFILE AND CARDIOVASCULAR RISK FACTORS IN PATIENTS WITH AUTOIMMUNE HYPOTHYROIDISM

summary: When formal proofs or deductive verifications exceed human cognitive surveyability, does epistemic justification require an agent-accessible chain of reasoning, or must epistemology shift from internalist warrant to structural-systemic reliability? Since the seventeenth-century rationalist and empiricist programs of Descartes and Locke, Western epistemology has rested upon the axiom of epistemic transparency: for an epistemic agent S to possess genuine a priori demonstrative knowledge of a theorem phi, S must be capable of cognitively surveying the inferential chain connecting primitive axioms Gamma to phi. Even when Bolzano, Frege, and Russell purged psychologism and spatio-temporal intuition from deductive logic, they treated formalization as a vehicle for rendering every inferential transition perspicuous to rational inspection. However, automated theorem provers, Boolean satisfiability (SAT) solvers, and interactive proof assistants routinely generate formal derivations that are deductively sound yet impossible for any finite biological mind to survey in full—violating the Wittgensteinian criterion of cognitive surveyability (Übersichtlichkeit). This paper provides a systematic formal and historical analysis of this problem across eight sections: (1) Section 1 reconstructs the classical transparency paradigm across Descartes, Leibniz, Locke, and Kant, isolating the working-memory and temporal synthesis bounds built into classical deductio; (2) Section 2 demonstrates how the Bolzanian-Fregean-Hilbertian quest for local step-wise gaplessness (Lückenlosigkeit) triggered an inverse scaling law that dialectically destroyed global proof surveyability; (3) Section 3 analyzes the Wittgensteinian critique of un-surveyable derivations, formalizing the distinction between a normative grammatical criterion and an empirical physical experiment; (4) Section 4 proves via Gödelian speed-up, Gentzen cut-elimination, and propositional proof complexity lower bounds that trans-surveyable derivations (||D|| >> kappa(S)) are an inescapable metamathematical feature of formal systems rather than an artifact of unoptimized proof search; (5) Section 5 introduces Bounded Justification Logic (BJL_kappa), formally deriving the inconsistency of the Classical Surveyability Trilemma; (6) Section 6 evaluates the Tymoczko–Burge–Kripke debate on computer-assisted proofs, refuting both quasi-empiricist hardware inductivism and ungrounded testimonial transmission; (7) Section 7 constructs a positive theory of Structural-Systemic Warrant (SSW), demonstrating how de Bruijn meta-kernel soundness compression and substrate-invariant equivalence preserve derivative a priori warrant while bifurcating demonstrative warrant (Dass-Wissen) from explanatory illumination (Warum-Wissen); (8) Section 8 addresses foundational objections from rule-following skepticism, Gödelian second-incompleteness limits, and zero-knowledge probabilistic verification (ZKPs and PCPs), synthesizing the general epistemological conclusions.

Since the seventeenth-century rationalist and empiricist programs of Descartes and Locke, Western epistemology has rested upon the axiom of epistemic transparency: for an epistemic agent S to possess genuine a priori demonstrative knowledge of a theorem phi, S must be capable of cognitively surveying the inferential chain connecting primitive axioms Gamma to phi. Even when Bolzano, Frege, and Russell purged psychologism and spatio-temporal intuition from deductive logic, they treated formalization as a vehicle for rendering every inferential transition perspicuous to rational inspection. However, automated theorem provers, Boolean satisfiability (SAT) solvers, and interactive proof assistants routinely generate formal derivations that are deductively sound yet impossible for any finite biological mind to survey in full—violating the Wittgensteinian criterion of cognitive surveyability (Übersichtlichkeit). This paper provides a systematic formal and historical analysis of this problem across eight sections: (1) Section 1 reconstructs the classical transparency paradigm across Descartes, Leibniz, Locke, and Kant, isolating the working-memory and temporal synthesis bounds built into classical deductio; (2) Section 2 demonstrates how the Bolzanian-Fregean-Hilbertian quest for local step-wise gaplessness (Lückenlosigkeit) triggered an inverse scaling law that dialectically destroyed global proof surveyability; (3) Section 3 analyzes the Wittgensteinian critique of un-surveyable derivations, formalizing the distinction between a normative grammatical criterion and an empirical physical experiment; (4) Section 4 proves via Gödelian speed-up, Gentzen cut-elimination, and propositional proof complexity lower bounds that trans-surveyable derivations (||D|| >> kappa(S)) are an inescapable metamathematical feature of formal systems rather than an artifact of unoptimized proof search; (5) Section 5 introduces Bounded Justification Logic (BJL_kappa), formally deriving the inconsistency of the Classical Surveyability Trilemma; (6) Section 6 evaluates the Tymoczko–Burge–Kripke debate on computer-assisted proofs, refuting both quasi-empiricist hardware inductivism and ungrounded testimonial transmission; (7) Section 7 constructs a positive theory of Structural-Systemic Warrant (SSW), demonstrating how de Bruijn meta-kernel soundness compression and substrate-invariant equivalence preserve derivative a priori warrant while bifurcating demonstrative warrant (Dass-Wissen) from explanatory illumination (Warum-Wissen); (8) Section 8 addresses foundational objections from rule-following skepticism, Gödelian second-incompleteness limits, and zero-knowledge probabilistic verification (ZKPs and PCPs), synthesizing the general epistemological conclusions.

summary: The book as a PDF, in the shape it is printed: read it in the browser at https://h0ffmann.github.io/closed-source/paper.pdf , or download it from the newest release at https://github.com/h0ffmann/closed-source/releases/latest/download/closed-source.pdf . The files of this record are the source that builds that PDF. A position paper arguing that closed source has failed as a protection, for science first. It reads the case through Robert M. Pirsig's Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance (1974), the book it stands on: the number of rational hypotheses that can explain a phenomenon is infinite, so science never closes, and a method that only its owner can open is one that nobody else can test. Large language models now decompile binaries into re-executable source; black-box queries extract parts of production models; distillation copies capabilities at industrial scale; and the largest 2026 trade-secret dispute in artificial intelligence, Apple's suit against OpenAI, turns on people, laptops and recruiting rather than on code that stayed secret. Against this background the paper revisits Linus Torvalds' Linux and Git as evidence that openness scales, and the author's closed undergraduate thesis as evidence of what secrecy costs a researcher. It argues that the ethical answer to universal reverse engineering is professional citation, proposes three rules for AI agents (borrow, cite, propagate), and describes Paper Fabric, the open pipeline in the Ouroboric style that produced it. This record is a book. It has not been peer reviewed. It holds the source of the book at the release tag: the Markdown text, the build and the agent configuration. The rendered PDFs are attached to the GitHub release of the same tag. The writer develops in the open. His three other works each have a permanent DOI, and this record cites all three: marola, an open, non-profit platform for sea conditions and bathing-water quality, written with five other people ( 10.5281/zenodo.23224155 ); WW3 GPU Lab, a bit-for-bit GPU port of WAVEWATCH III ( 10.5281/zenodo.23221351 ); and picasso, Nix flakes for scientific and agentic toolchains, which builds this book ( 10.5281/zenodo.23311208 ). The book is made in the Ouroboric style, and the Ouroboric ideas are Bruno Valério's ( https://github.com/ouroboric-dev/ouroboric ); Ouroboric has no DOI yet, so this record cites it by its address.

summary: A staged, reproducible pipeline for VLT/MUSE narrow-field-mode integral-field data: raw-cube reduction, spectral extraction of a faint companion next to a much brighter primary star with six independent extraction schemes, and hydrogen-line accretion analysis with detection limits calibrated against empirical nulls from control positions processed identically to the object. Every stage emits a machine-readable quality-control document, and later stages read those documents rather than trusting assumptions; provenance (input cube, SHA-256 hashes, specification version, wavelength frame, flux unit) travels with the products. Research code under active development. This is the version used in Ramírez Reyes & Cáceres (in preparation).

summary: This deposit contains the data, code, and figures underlying a study of owned dog and cat populations in Ecuador, reconstructed from the 2022 Population and Housing Census (Censo de Población y Vivienda, CPV 2022) of the National Institute of Statistics and Censuses (INEC). It includes: (i) indicator tables of dog and cat ownership at the province, canton, and parish levels (CSV), with derived indicators such as the percentage of households keeping pets, pets per capita, and the dog-to-cat ratio; (ii) geospatial layers (GeoPackage) joining these indicators to canton and parish boundaries, plus the local spatial-cluster (LISA) classification; (iii) the full analysis pipeline (Python) that builds the indicators from the primary census tabulations, harmonizes place names and geometries, runs the spatial analysis, and generates the figures; (iv) the five manuscript figures (TIFF, 300 dpi); and (v) a documented log of figures on companion-animal populations circulated in Ecuadorian media and official communications, compared with the values reconstructed here. At the national level, the census records 7,601,269 owned dogs and cats (5,211,037 dogs and 2,390,232 cats), with 58.3% of households keeping at least one. Ownership is markedly higher in rural areas and strongly clustered across the central-southern Sierra (global Moran's I = 0.57). Raw inputs are not all redistributed here for licensing reasons; see the README and SOURCES file for provenance, licensing, and instructions to reproduce the analysis. title: Household dog and cat populations in Ecuador from the 2022 census: indicator datasets, spatial analysis, and figures

summary: This deposit contains the data, code, and figures underlying a study of owned dog and cat populations in Ecuador, reconstructed from the 2022 Population and Housing Census (Censo de Población y Vivienda, CPV 2022) of the National Institute of Statistics and Censuses (INEC). It includes: (i) indicator tables of dog and cat ownership at the province, canton, and parish levels (CSV), with derived indicators such as the percentage of households keeping pets, pets per capita, and the dog-to-cat ratio; (ii) geospatial layers (GeoPackage) joining these indicators to canton and parish boundaries, plus the local spatial-cluster (LISA) classification; (iii) the full analysis pipeline (Python) that builds the indicators from the primary census tabulations, harmonizes place names and geometries, runs the spatial analysis, and generates the figures; (iv) the five manuscript figures (TIFF, 300 dpi); and (v) a documented log of figures on companion-animal populations circulated in Ecuadorian media and official communications, compared with the values reconstructed here. At the national level, the census records 7,601,269 owned dogs and cats (5,211,037 dogs and 2,390,232 cats), with 58.3% of households keeping at least one. Ownership is markedly higher in rural areas and strongly clustered across the central-southern Sierra (global Moran's I = 0.57). summary: EXTERNAL QIGONG AND HUMAN THERMAL RADIATION PATTERNS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English research working monograph investigating whether thermographic differences observed during culturally defined qigong and matched neutral tasks can be distinguished from ordinary human thermoregulation, environmental exchange and measurement bias. The governing three-coupling is infrared thermal imaging x physiological regulation x heat-transfer models. The research treats “external qi” as a cultural and experimental task label, not an established physical energy carrier. The scientific core separates raw infrared radiance from inferred skin temperature and estimated heat flux. It develops emissivity and reflected-wall correction, blackbody calibration, spectral detector response, conduction and perfusion bioheat models, convection, evaporation, respiration-related temperature patterns, posture and muscular activity. The original candidate bulk heat equation is explicitly refined by separating volumetric tissue transport from surface heat-transfer boundary conditions. The principal proposed test uses concealed task assignments, matched breathing/movement/clothing, phantom references, negative-control regions and conventional physics-first rivals. Thirty physically distinct mathematical plates document governing relationships, units, assumptions, identifiability, masked falsifiers and chapter links. Eighty-two independent research chapters contain 410 single-page investigations. The true center of the monograph is its 200 one-page Research Gates, each posing a falsifiable question in bold deep-navy typography and asking what an independent successor must measure, challenge, disprove or preserve. Thirty-three differentiated Phoenix Answer Embryos propose future instruments, error-correction artifacts, negative-result protocols and reproducibility tools. The DOI registry separates three STARLI author mother volumes from eleven externally published methodological or conventional-science references on infrared thermography, emissivity, classical bioheat and research design. Bibliographic sources constrain methods; they do not validate extraordinary qigong mechanisms. Every integrated experiment is prospective. The book presents no completed human intervention, clinically established effect, new physical particle or evidence of treatment efficacy. Ethical authorization and independent scientific review would be required before future human-observation research. summary: EXTERNAL QIGONG AND HUMAN THERMAL RADIATION PATTERNS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English research working monograph investigating whether thermographic differences observed during culturally defined qigong and matched neutral tasks can be distinguished from ordinary human thermoregulation, environmental exchange and measurement bias. The governing three-coupling is infrared thermal imaging x physiological regulation x heat-transfer models. The research treats “external qi” as a cultural and experimental task label, not an established physical energy carrier. The scientific core separates raw infrared radiance from inferred skin temperature and estimated heat flux. It develops emissivity and reflected-wall correction, blackbody calibration, spectral detector response, conduction and perfusion bioheat models, convection, evaporation, respiration-related temperature patterns, posture and muscular activity. The original candidate bulk heat equation is explicitly refined by separating volumetric tissue transport from surface heat-transfer boundary conditions. The principal proposed test uses concealed task assignments, matched breathing/movement/clothing, phantom references, negative-control regions and conventional physics-first rivals. Thirty physically distinct mathematical plates document governing relationships, units, assumptions, identifiability, masked falsifiers and chapter links. Eighty-two independent research chapters contain 410 single-page investigations. The true center of the monograph is its 200 one-page Research Gates, each posing a falsifiable question in bold deep-navy typography and asking what an independent successor must measure, challenge, disprove or preserve. Thirty-three differentiated Phoenix Answer Embryos propose future instruments, error-correction artifacts, negative-result protocols and reproducibility tools. The DOI registry separates three STARLI author mother volumes from eleven externally published methodological or conventional-science references on infrared thermography, emissivity, classical bioheat and research design. Bibliographic sources constrain methods; they do not validate extraordinary qigong mechanisms. Every integrated experiment is prospective. The book presents no completed human intervention, clinically established effect, new physical particle or evidence of treatment efficacy. Ethical authorization and independent scientific review would be required before future human-observation research. summary: Human observers can encounter representations of the same relational contribution history yet form different beliefs about its significance and trustworthiness. This third paper in a coordinated research programme investigates cognitive processes between the structural availability of evidence and an observer’s assessment of a person, claim, or contribution. Its proposed analytic objects are selective attention, evidence encoding, reconstructive memory, attribution, interpretive schemas, belief revision, epistemic vigilance, and behavioral reliance. The inquiry distinguishes evidentiary accessibility from cognitive encounter, subjective confidence from justified assessment, and expressed trust from risk-bearing cooperation. Prior work in attention, working memory, judgment under uncertainty, epistemic vigilance, and trust in automation motivates a provisional sequential-kernel architecture; that architecture remains a research proposal rather than a validated general cognitive model. AI-mediated information environments supply a historically relevant application, without defining the paper’s full scope. This working draft contains all ten planned sections, covering cognitive interfaces, selective attention, memory-based trajectory reconstruction, contribution attribution, proposition-specific belief revision, testimony evaluation, behavioral reliance, empirical designs with explicit identification boundaries, and a synthesis of conditional theoretical findings. It reports no original empirical results.
title: Cognitive Mediation of Relational Evidence: An Investigation of Epistemic Judgment and Reliance

summary: Timely state updates are essential for coordination and monitoring in multi-agent systems, such as teams of mobile robots exchanging state information. When agents share a wireless channel, collisions and slow convergence of distributed access schemes can degrade information freshness over finite operating periods. This paper proposes age-threshold frame-based random access (AFRA), a distributed medium access control protocol for minimizing age of information (AoI). Once its age reaches a threshold, an agent starts a local frame with a mandatory transmission and, if unsuccessful, makes one further attempt at a uniformly selected remaining slot. Each attempt carries a freshly generated update. AFRA requires only local state and acknowledgment feedback, with shared slot boundaries but independently timed local frames. We prove almost-sure convergence from any legal initial state to collision-free periodic operation when the frame length $L$ and age threshold $T$ satisfy $L\ge T>N\ge2$, where $N$ is the number of agents. We also derive closed-form expressions for steady-state throughput, average AoI, and average peak AoI. Simulations demonstrate that AFRA combines rapid convergence at small age thresholds with lower window-averaged AoI than the existing age-aware random access schemes evaluated in this study.
title: AFRA: Age-Threshold Frame-Based Random Access for Timely Communication in Multi-Agent Systems

summary: A Turing machine carries a computation forward through successive configurations, but continuation beyond infinitely many steps requires a rule assigning the configuration from which the next instruction can proceed. The Quantum Γ-Turing machine considered here retains a finite-dimensional register’s trace-norm limit when it exists, preserving the coherence needed by subsequent operations. Averaging a history that never settles permits another continuation, although registers independent at every finite stage can then acquire correlations through their shared timing. We characterise when an assigned state can replace its history without changing a later joint calculation. For assignments compatible with every fixed quantum operation, the largest composition error equals the mean trace-norm distance from the assigned state, and a partner carrying classical labels can approach that value. Independent composition with every partner holds precisely when temporal variance under the chosen mean vanishes. Requiring this under every shift-invariant mean gives uniform vanishing of average squared fluctuations, a condition that permits sparse excursions despite failure of ordinary convergence. For a programme repeatedly applying one fixed channel, independent composition is instead equivalent to ordinary convergence, with the exact error determined by its surviving nonstationary spectral component. Algebraically specified channels and initial states admit a finite decision procedure and certified bounds, while bounded repetitions of states preserve the stronger averaging condition and transfer its certificates to a simulation. These results connect transfinite continuation to finite verification for specified programmes and provide composition certificates that can be carried through a controlled simulation.
title: Independent Composition and Quantum Limits in Transfinite Γ-Turing Machines

summary: Per distruggere la Rotta dei Chersoneso, venne fatta la Battaglia di Cheronea https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battaglia_di_Cheronea_(87_a.C.) Per distruggere i commerci con Etruschi e Cartaginesi, venne fatta la Battaglia di Alalia https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battaglia_del_Mare_Sardo Per distruggere i rapporti con la Facies Sarda dei Bessi di Perperikon, venne fatta la battaglia del Monte Emo:   La battaglia del Monte Emo (o Haemus ) è storicamente legata a due momenti distinti dell'antichità che videro scontrarsi gli eserciti invasori con le tribù tracie, in particolare i Bessi , e il cui contesto geografico e spirituale è strettamente connesso al celebre sito monumentale di Perperikon , situato nelle montagne dei Rodopi in Bulgaria. [ 1 , 2 ] Ecco come si collegano questi tre elementi:   1. La prima battaglia del Monte Emo (335 a.C.) Prima di lanciare la sua campagna contro i Persiani, Alessandro Magno guidò una spedizione nei Balcani per rendere sicuri i confini settentrionali del suo regno. Sul Monte Emo (l'attuale catena dei Monti Balcani) affrontò i Traci Liberi e altre tribù locali. [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] La tattica dei carri: I Traci si erano posizionati sulla vetta e intendevano far rotolare dei pesanti carri giù dai ripidi pendii per rompere la falange macedone. [ 1 , 2 ] La contromossa di Alessandro: Il re macedone ordinò ai suoi soldati di aprire i ranghi per far passare i carri oppure di sdraiarsi a terra coprendosi con gli scudi intersecati (creando una sorta di testuggine). La tattica funzionò alla perfezione: i carri rimbalzarono sugli scudi senza causare vittime tra i Macedoni. Le truppe di Alessandro caricarono poi la vetta, sbaragliando i difensori. [ 1 , 2 , 3 ]   2. Lo scontro dei Bessi con Roma (72 a.C.) In epoca successiva, il nome della battaglia del Monte Emo si associa alla sottomissione definitiva dei Bessi , una delle tribù tracie più bellicose e fanaticamente dedite al culto religioso. Il proconsole romano Marco Licinio Lucullo affrontò i Bessi proprio nei pressi della catena del Monte Emo, sconfiggendoli duramente in una grande battaglia campale, conquistando il loro centro principale ( Uscudama ) e aprendo la strada alla successiva egemonia romana nella regione. [ 1 , 2 , 3 ]   3. Il legame con Perperikon La tribù dei Bessi era storicamente la custode del famosissimo Santuario e Oracolo di Dioniso , situato proprio sulla maestosa roccia sacra di Perperikon . Questo luogo ha un valore storico eccezionale per due importanti profezie collegate ai protagonisti di queste guerre: [ 1 , 2 ] La profezia di Alessandro Magno: Secondo le fonti antiche, prima di iniziare la sua spedizione in Asia (subito dopo aver pacificato la Tracia), Alessandro visitò l'oracolo di Dioniso a Perperikon. Il vino versato sull'altare creò una fiammata altissima fino al cielo, un segno divino che i sacerdoti interpretarono come il presagio che avrebbe conquistato il mondo intero. [ 1 ] La profezia di Ottaviano Augusto: Anni dopo, anche il padre di Augusto (Gaio Ottavio) ricevette nello stesso santuario dei Bessi la medesima profezia sul futuro dominio globale di suo figlio. [ 1 ] In sintesi, la resistenza dei Traci sul Monte Emo rappresenta lo scontro militare per il controllo dei Balcani, mentre Perperikon costituisce il cuore spirituale, politico e identitario della tribù dei Bessi che contro quegli imperi tentò invano di difendere la propria indipendenza. [ 1 , 2 ]   Attenzione: questo documento è stato appena pensato: si tratta di una bozza iniziale basata sul Paradigma Sardo Corso Atlantideo di Luigi Usai. Verrà corretto ed espanso nel tempo, come tutti gli altri lavori di Usai Luigi.     {"@context":{"ra":"https://www.luigiusai.it/ontology/rotta-aristeica/index.html#","rotta":"https://www.luigiusai.it/ontology/rotta-aristeica/","schema":"https://schema.org/"

summary: Deepwave provides wave propagation modules for PyTorch, for applications such as seismic imaging and inversion. It performs forward modelling and backpropagation, so it can simulate wave propagation to generate synthetic data, or invert for the scattering potential (reverse-time migration, RTM, or its least-squares counterpart, LSRTM), other model parameters (full-waveform inversion, FWI), initial wavefields, or source wavelets. It can also be used inside a larger chain of operations, with forward and backpropagation flowing through the whole chain end to end. You can use your own objective functions, or functions that generate the propagator's inputs, and PyTorch's automatic differentiation calculates how to backpropagate through them. New to seismic/wave-equation terminology? The glossary defines the terms (PML, CFL, Born, FWI, and more) used throughout this README and the rest of the documentation. Deepwave requires Python 3.9 or later and PyTorch 2.4 or later. First install PyTorch for your CPU or CUDA device using the instructions on the PyTorch website . Then install Deepwave: pip install deepwave   macOS wheels support Apple Silicon. Intel Mac wheels are no longer provided: PyTorch 2.4 and newer do not publish wheels for that platform. Prebuilt x86 wheels require AVX2. Older CPUs need a source build; see installation troubleshooting . PyTorch is Deepwave's only dependency. The example scripts under docs/ additionally import matplotlib (to draw their figures) and, in some cases, numpy , scipy (smoothing and filter design), torchaudio (applying those filters), torchvision and geomloss , but those are needed only to run the examples, never by Deepwave itself. To install all of them: pip install 'deepwave[examples]'   The documentation contains examples and instructions on how to install and use Deepwave. You might also like to watch a video summary of Deepwave . Not every propagator supports every option (dimensionality, backend, boundary faces, batching, second-order differentiation, callbacks, ...). See the capability matrix (declared in the code and checked by conformance tests) before assuming a combination works. Why Deepwave Computationally efficient. Deepwave's compiled kernels use a hand-derived adjoint for better performance and lower memory requirements than pure PyTorch implementations. See what Deepwave calculates . Second derivatives are supported, not just first. The scalar, acoustic, and elastic propagators can compute Hessian-vector products (derivatives of gradients); see the Hessian example . Born (linearised) modelling. Model scattered waves from perturbations to a background medium for linearised inversion and imaging. See the torch.func example . Deepwave fits into an ordinary PyTorch workflow. Because propagation is a normal PyTorch autograd Function , it works directly with PyTorch optimisers, DistributedDataParallel over shots, torch.func transforms, and any PyTorch loss function or neural-network model of the input parameters. See the capability matrix for exactly what each propagator supports. Deepwave does not try to be a general symbolic PDE solver, a multi-node HPC code, or a non-differentiable simulation toolkit — see Devito , SPECFEM , and k-Wave respectively for those needs. If you are choosing between wave-propagation packages, see the comparison guide . (Note: the DeepWave-KAUST GitHub organisation, home of the SWEEP package, is unrelated to this project.) Features Supports the 1D, 2D, and 3D constant density acoustic / scalar wave equation (regular and Born modelling), variable density acoustic, elastic, viscoacoustic (single-mechanism SLS attenuation), elastic VTI (anisotropic), and pseudo-acoustic VTI ( deepwave.acoustic_vti , the Duveneck et al. 2008 V_S=0 reduction) wave equations Runs on CPUs and appropriate GPUs The gradient of all outputs (final wavefields and receiver data) can be calculated with respect to the model parameters (wavespeed, scattering potential, etc
title: Deepwave

summary: Data and R code that reproduce all tables and figures of the article "Dependence on China, Export Volatility and Relationship Persistence: Shipment-Level Evidence from Peruvian Copper Ore, 2006–2025", of its Appendix A and of its Supplementary Material.   Version 1.1.0 accompanies the revised manuscript (first review round). It keeps all data, code and outputs of version 1.0.0, which are reproduced identically, and adds the scripts, data and outputs of the analyses carried out in the revision: Cox models stratified by firm, with shared frailty and with a firm random effect, and without Chinese-owned firms; a firm-level (granular) and a Shapley decomposition of aggregate export volatility; a destination counterfactual; seasonality checks; regime-specific concentration coefficients; destination concentration by net weight; sensitivity analyses and a shift-share instrument for the firm–year panel; mirror statistics from UN Comtrade (imports of HS 2603 reported by China and the Republic of Korea); and a comparison of the extract with SUNAT's published statistics (Tables G8 and G9).   The package contains the shipment-level extract of Peruvian exports of copper ores and concentrates (HS 2603.00.00.00) from PromPerú's Infotrade platform, based on SUNAT export customs declarations, January 2006 – December 2025, validated month by month against PromPerú's official totals (23,106 shipments; 22,582 commercial shipments by 200 firms to 44 destinations, USD 219.3 billion FOB, in the analysis), together with the auxiliary data, the processed datasets and all outputs. A single script (run_all.R) runs the whole pipeline.   Exporters who are natural persons (18 of 266 RUCs; 90 shipments) are pseudonymized; the replacement is one-to-one and does not change any result. The firm–destination–month dataset obtained from SUNAT through an access-to-information request, used only for cross-validation, is not redistributed. See README.md for details.
title: Data and R code for: Dependence on China, Export Volatility and Relationship Persistence: Shipment-Level Evidence from Peruvian Copper Ore, 2006–2025

summary: Öz   Bu çalışmanın amacı, genç erkek basketbolcularda Fonksiyonel Hareket Tarama (FMS) toplam ve alt test puanları ile alt ekstremite denge asimetrisi arasındaki ilişkileri ve bu puanların asimetriyi yordama düzeyini incelemektir. Kesitsel ve ilişkisel tarama modelinde tasarlanan araştırmaya, yaş ortalaması 18,90 ± 1,21 yıl ve spor yaşı ortalaması 7,83 ± 1,77 yıl olan 52 gönüllü lisanslı erkek basketbolcu katılmıştır. Fonksiyonel hareketler yedi alt testten oluşan FMS ile değerlendirilmiştir. Alt testler 0–3 arasında puanlanmış ve toplam puan 21 puan üzerinden değerlendirilmiştir. Dinamik denge, anterior, posteromedial ve posterolateral uzanma yönlerini içeren Y-Denge Testi (YBT) ile ölçülmüştür. Her iki alt ekstremiteden elde edilen uzanma mesafeleri kullanılarak taraflara ait bileşik puanlar hesaplanmış ve denge asimetri yüzdesi analiz edilmiştir. Verilerin analizinde betimsel istatistikler, Pearson korelasyon analizi ve çoklu doğrusal regresyon analizi kullanılmıştır. FMS toplam puanı ile asimetri yüzdesi (r = −0,059), dominant bileşik puan (r = −0,031) ve non-dominant bileşik puan (r = −0,013) arasında anlamlı ilişki bulunmamıştır (p > 0,05). Asimetri yüzdesi ile dominant bileşik puan arasında çok güçlü pozitif ilişki saptanmıştır (r = 0,921; p < 0,01). FMS toplam ve alt test puanlarını içeren regresyon modeli genel olarak anlamlı değildir (R² = 0,256; düzeltilmiş R² = 0,117; p = 0,094). Modelde gövde stabilitesi şınavının (TSPU) katsayısı negatif (β = −0,399; p = 0,015), omuz mobilitesinin (SM) katsayısı ise pozitif yönde anlamlı bulunmuştur (β = 0,342; p = 0,049). Diğer alt testlerin ve toplam puanın katsayıları anlamlı değildir (p > 0,05). Sonuç olarak, FMS toplam puanı bu örneklemde denge asimetrisiyle anlamlı bir ilişki göstermemiştir. Bulgular, basketbolcuların değerlendirilmesinde yalnızca toplam FMS puanına odaklanılmaması gerektiğini; alt test sonuçlarının ve taraflara özgü dinamik denge ölçümlerinin birlikte ele alınması gerektiğini göstermektedir.   Anahtar Kelimeler: Basketbol, Fonksiyonel Hareket Taraması, Dinamik Denge, Ekstremiteler Arası Asimetri, Gövde Stabilitesi   Abstract The relationship between the Functional Movement Screen (FMS) total and individual test scores and the asymmetry of balance of the lower extremities, as well as the predictive effect on young male basketball players, was analysed in this study. This was a cross-sectional correlational study that consisted of 52 licensed male basketball players volunteering for the study at the age of 18.90 ± 1.21 years and having a sport experience of 7.83 ± 1.77 years. The assessment of functional movement was carried out through the seven FMS tests. These tests were individually scored in range of 0 to 3 points with a maximal total of 21 points. Reach distances for both lower extremities were used to calculate limb-specific composite scores, and balance asymmetry percentage was analyzed. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression were used. FMS total score was not significantly correlated with asymmetry percentage (r = −0.059), dominant composite score (r = −0.031), or non-dominant composite score (r = −0.013; all p > 0.05). Asymmetry percentage showed a very strong positive correlation with dominant composite score (r = 0.921; p < 0.01). The regression model including FMS total and individual test scores was not statistically significant overall (R² = 0.256; adjusted R² = 0.117; p = 0.094). summary: This record preserves the v0.2.0 trained-model weight bundle for takotsubo_ami_ai_ecg. It contains selected ViT, ConvNeXtV2 and MLP-Mixer inference tensors in safetensors format, ViT configuration files, a manifest, and the applicable license texts and notices. These research models classify prepared ECG images as takotsubo syndrome or acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). summary: Replication package for the paper "Risk, not sunshine: financing costs drive the price of reliable solar-plus-storage electricity in the Middle East and North Africa" (Younas Khan and Štefan Bojnec). WHAT THIS IS Code, input data, result tables, figures and a supplementary data workbook for an hourly solar-plus-battery cost comparison of 19 Middle East and North African countries (24 sites: the 19 capitals plus five interior desert sites). The study decomposes the cross-country cost gap into cost of capital, regional equipment price and solar yield, and tests the result against finance shocks, 24 weather years, CMIP6 climate change and Monte Carlo uncertainty. The manuscript itself is not part of this deposit. CONTENTS - code/: all analysis scripts (photovoltaic model, hourly dispatch and design search, climate factors, 24-weather-year test, build-out link, decomposition, bootstrap, Monte Carlo, figures, supplementary tables) and run_all.sh, which reproduces everything in about 6 minutes on one core. - data/inputs/: the input data the scripts read (NASA POWER weather, CMIP6 point extracts, IRENA and SIPRI data, demand and footprint indicators). - results/: result tables (CSV) and results.json, which holds every number quoted in the paper. - outputs/Supplementary_Data.xlsx: a workbook with one sheet for each supplementary table (S1–S26). - outputs/figures/: the figures generated by the code (PNG and PDF). - README.md: step-by-step instructions, a map from each figure and table to its script, and the provenance and terms of each input file. HOW TO REUSE Install the packages in requirements.txt (Python 3.13), then run ./run_all.sh. All random draws use fixed seeds, so a rerun with the default 2,000 Monte Carlo draws reproduces results.json. LICENCE AND THIRD-PARTY DATA The code is released under the MIT licence and the derived results and workbook under CC BY 4.0. Input files from NASA POWER, IRENA, SIPRI, Ember and the Copernicus Climate Data Store keep the terms of their providers and must be cited to the original sources (see README.md). KNOWN LIMITS Costs of capital for Algeria, Libya, Palestine, Syria and Yemen and all hydrogen-chain costs are placeholders; hourly load is assumed, not measured; each country is represented by one reference site. These are documented in Supplementary Tables S20–S22. VERSIONS Version 1.1.0 contains the files listed above. Further datasets will be added as new versions of this record or as separate records linked to it.
